origin.description: This function creates colors of class LAB; a subclass of the virtual color class.

arguments.name: L, A, B
arguments.text: L, a, and b coordinates. Separate vectors or a three-column matrix passed as L.

arguments.name: names
arguments.text: Row names for the colors. By default the row names of L are used.

origin.details: L is luminance between 0 and 100; a and b are typically between -100 and 100 but may exceed that for highly saturated colors. LAB is a perceptual transformation of CIE XYZ.
origin.value: An object of class LAB which inherits from class color. The coords slot is a matrix with columns L, A, and B.

translation.description: This function creates colors of class LAB; a subclass of the virtual color class.

arguments.name: L, A, B
arguments.text: L, a, and b as separate arrays or scalars, or an n by 3 matrix as L when A and B are omitted. Scalars for A or B recycle to the length of L.

arguments.name: names
arguments.text: Row names. When L is a (matrix, rownames) pair, row names default from the pair if names is omitted.

translation.details: L is luminance between 0 and 100; a and b are typically between -100 and 100. Calling LAB() with no L returns an empty LAB object. A matrix that is not n by 3, or a length mismatch after recycling, raises invalid color matrix.
translation.value: A LABColor object. space is LAB, coords is an n by 3 float64 array with columns L, A, and B, and names is the row names or None.
translation.example:
from colorspace.lab import LAB
import numpy as np

print(LAB(np.linspace(0, 100, 13)[:-1], 0, 0))
